title: Penny Dreadfuls: 1800s Trash Horror Comics
hook: Aristocrats panicked over cheap 1-penny serial horror stories.

scenes.text: In the 1830s, cheap steam-powered printing presses revolutionized literature, creating the world's first mass-market teenage fiction.

scenes.voicedText: In the 1830s, cheap steam-powered printing presses revolutionized literature, creating the world's first mass-market teenage fiction.

scenes.text: Called 'Penny Bloods' or 'Penny Dreadfuls', they were weekly eight-page serials sold for just one single copper penny to working-class boys.
scenes.imagePrompt: Victorian newsagent stall counter with stacks of woodcut-illustrated pamphlets, open newspapers, and glass jars of lemon drops. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Called 'Penny Bloods' or 'Penny Dreadfuls', they were weekly eight-page serials sold for just one single copper penny to working-class boys.

scenes.text: They featured sensational, gory tales of razor-wielding fiends like Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street, and Varney the Vampire.

scenes.voicedText: They featured sensational, gory tales of razor-wielding fiends like Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street, and Varney the Vampire.

scenes.text: Upper-class Victorian critics panicked, claiming these trashy thrillers were corrupting youth and turning factory boys into ruthless street criminals.

scenes.text: Despite moral outrage, millions were sold, establishing the origins of modern comic books, superhero serials, and detective mysteries.
